summary: This informational memo gathers the terms used to talk about provider-provisioned virtual private networks, where a service provider runs the VPN for customers. Several IETF working groups had proposed overlapping solutions, so the document sets a common vocabulary to avoid confusion.

eli5.summary: When many people build similar things, they often call them different names. This document is a word list that makes everyone use the same names for VPNs run by a network company.

questions: what is a l2vpn or l3vpn
what is a provider provisioned vpn
what is the difference between vpls and vpws
subtitle: A shared vocabulary for VPNs that a service provider builds and runs for its customers.

tldr.problem: Many proposals for provider-provisioned VPNs overlapped, and in places one term covered several concepts while several terms covered one concept.
tldr.mechanism: The memo gathers the services, building blocks, functions, devices and network terms of the area, says which names have been replaced, and groups VPNs into a taxonomy of Layer 2 and Layer 3 types.
tldr.outcome: It gives the L2VPN and L3VPN working groups a common foundation for their terminology. It is informational and defines no protocol.

today: RFC 4026 is an Informational document, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It records terminology as of its time, and it marks several of its own entries as dated or replaced.

sections.title: Why a Common Vocabulary
sections.content:
A comparatively large number of memos went to the former PPVPN working group and to the L2VPN, L3VPN and PWE3 working groups. They all addressed provider provisioned virtual private networking for end customers, and there was a great deal of commonality among the proposed solutions. The result was a partial set of new concepts in which more than one term covered the same concept and sometimes the same term covered more than one.

This RFC proposes a foundation for a unified terminology for the L2VPN and L3VPN groups, using the parallel PWE3 concepts as references where useful. Its stated aim is to fully cover the concepts in the core L2VPN and L3VPN documents, and it tries to cite the earliest uses of the terms. The material is arranged as services, building blocks, functions and typical devices.
sections.eli5: Everyone was calling the same thing by different names, so this document picks the names and writes them down.

sections.title: The Services
sections.content:
A Layer 3 VPN (L3VPN) interconnects hosts and routers based on Layer 3 addresses. A Layer 2 VPN (L2VPN) comes in three types in this document: VPWS, VPLS and IPLS.

A Virtual Private Wire Service (VPWS) is a point-to-point circuit between two CE devices, built across a packet switched network. The CE connects to a PE over an attachment circuit, and the PEs are joined by a pseudo wire. A Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) emulates a traditional LAN: remote LAN segments behave as one LAN, and the provider network emulates a learning bridge that forwards on MAC addresses, or MAC addresses and VLAN tag. The VPLS is point to multipoint and the VPWS is point to point. An IP-only LAN-like Service (IPLS) is very like a VPLS, but the CE devices are hosts or routers, and the service carries only IP packets plus supporting packets such as ICMP and ARP, both IPv4 and IPv6.

Other entries record history. Transparent LAN Service (TLS) was an early name for VPLS, and VLLS and VPSN were replaced by VPWS and VPLS. The generic term VPN covers the use of public or private networks to create groups of users separated from other users that can communicate as if on a private network. Stronger separation such as end-to-end encryption is outside the scope of the IETF VPN working group charters.
sections.eli5: A private line between two houses is one kind of service. A pretend shared room that joins houses in different towns is another. The words tell you which one someone means.

sections.title: Classifying VPNs
sections.content:
The memo reproduces a taxonomy from RFC 3809. At the top are Layer 2 and Layer 3 VPNs. Layer 2 splits into point-to-point (VPWS) and point-to-multipoint (VPLS, IPLS). Layer 3 splits into PE-based and CE-based.

In a CE-based VPN the provider network has no knowledge of the customer VPN. All VPN procedures run in the CE devices, and the PEs do not know the traffic is VPN traffic. In a PE-based VPN the PE maintains the VPN state and isolates one VPN from another, so the CE needs no changes to connect to a provider VPN instead of a private network. The PEs forward through tunnels based on the destination IP address, and the tunnels may use GRE, IP-in-IP, IPsec or MPLS.

Two PE-based styles are named. In the Virtual Router style the PE keeps a complete logical router per VPN, each with its own forwarding table and routing protocol instance. In BGP/MPLS IP VPNs the PE keeps a separate forwarding table per VPN while running a single BGP instance, marking route advertisements with attributes that identify the VPN. The older name "RFC 2547 style" was replaced by BGP/MPLS IP VPNs.
sections.eli5: Some private networks are built by the customer with the provider just moving the packets, and some are built by the provider so the customer sees nothing different. The document names both kinds.

sections.title: Building Blocks: CE, PE and P
sections.content:
The CE is the device with the functionality needed on the customer premises to reach the service. It can be named by device, as a CE router (CE-R) or CE switch (CE-S), or by service, as an L3VPN-CE, VPLS-CE or VPWS-CE. A CE-R is a router in the customer network facing the provider, and a CE-S is a service-aware L2 switch. One router may be both an L2VPN-CE and an L3VPN-CE.

The PE is the device or set of devices at the provider edge with the functionality to interface with the customer. It can be a PE router (PE-R, a L3 device taking part in PSN routing) or a PE switch (PE-S, a L2 device), and it can be named by service as L3VPN-PE, VPWS-PE or VPLS-PE. For scaling, VPLS or VPWS functions can be split: the User facing PE (U-PE) takes forwarding decisions at the ingress, close to the customer, while the Network facing PE (N-PE) handles signalling and control. A P router is in the core with no interfaces directly toward a customer, so it keeps no VPN state and is VPN unaware.

The RFC warns that these blocks are an oversimplification of boxes: any of them could be spread across more than one physical box. It also lists names from specific Internet drafts, such as L2PE, LPE, PE-CLE, PE-Core, PE-Edge, PE-POP and VPLS Edge (VE), noting which are dated.
sections.eli5: The customer's door device, the provider's door device, and the plain roads in the middle each have their own name. Roads in the middle do not need to know whose packages they carry.

sections.title: Functions, Boxes and Network Terms
sections.content:
The functions include the attachment circuit (a physical or logical link joining a CE to a PE), backdoor links (links between CEs provided by the customer rather than the provider), and endpoint discovery, by which devices find all customer-facing ports in a service. For L2 services, flooding sends a frame with an unknown destination MAC address out of every other interface, and MAC address learning records the source address against the interface. Learning is qualified when it uses the MAC address and VLAN tag, and unqualified when it uses the MAC address only. Signalling lets PEs exchange information to set up PWs, PSN tunnels and tunnel multiplexers, automatically or by manual configuration.

The typical boxes are the aggregation box (a service-unaware L2 switch), the customer premises equipment or CPE (placed with the customer for connectivity monitoring), and the multi-tenant unit or MTU (an L2 switch in a building with several customers). The RFC says CPE and MTU should not be used in protocol specifications, and MTU also abbreviates Maximum Transmit Units.

The network terms start with the PSN, the network in which the tunnels for the VPN services are set up. A tunnel carries traffic from one PE to another, and a tunnel multiplexor sent with each packet says which service instance it belongs to. With MPLS this is a VC label, also called an inner label. A Route Distinguisher is an 8-byte value that, with a 4 byte IPv4 address, identifies a VPN-IPv4 address family. A Route Target is a BGP extended community identifying a set of sites, or more precisely a set of VRFs. A VRF is a per-site forwarding table on a PE. The memo also defines VFI, VSI (a virtual switching instance that serves one single VPLS) and Virtual Router.
sections.eli5: This part is the small print: how a device learns which door belongs to which address, what labels go on packages in the shared road, and what each type of box is called.
